content:
The "transition generation" typically refers to individuals born between 1943 and 1960, who were affected by changes in pension regulations during their working and retirement years.

Regarding the impact of early payment of the AHV (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung, or Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) pension: If an AHV pension is paid early (i.e., before the full retirement age), the pension amount is reduced. The reduction is proportional to the number of months by which the pension is claimed early. Conversely, delaying the payment of the pension beyond the full retirement age generally results in an increased pension amount.
